acceptance: An autouse module-scoped guard fails the module that leaves benchbox logger level or handlers, the quiet flag or the tracer provider changed, naming the state that leaked
INC-15's leak (the docs-export fixture before #3385) is caught by the guard without relying on the test that later observed it
The full fast and medium suites pass with the guard on, and any existing leaks it finds are fixed in the same change
context:
NOTE 2026-10-25: a further instance of cross-test sharing was fixed in PR #3442 (merge 39d54c8e6): every xdist worker inherited the controller's BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR and shared one benchmark_runs/datagen cache, so a nameless benchmark's DataFrame conversion (unknown_sf001/parquet/v8) on one worker pruned files another worker's joinorder test was reading (CI runs 40160396702, 40170713453, 40172922400). tests/utilities/session_isolation.py now gives each worker its own benchmark_runs root unless the user set BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR; test_each_parallel_worker_owns_its_benchmark_runs_root pins it. Consider covering shared output roots in this guard.

Source: classification of every Trunk push run on develop from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-24 (recorded on trunk-red-run-triage-20261024; incident ids refer to that table).
description: Two incidents (INC-15, 16; 6 red Trunk runs) were cross-test state leaking through module or session fixtures, exposed only by worker placement: a module-scoped docs-export fixture left the benchbox logger at ERROR (fixed in #3385), and chDB sessions held open across modules (fixed in #3423, which added an autouse module guard for open chDB connections). The same class recurred after test-logging-and-session-isolation-leaks-20261014. Extend the guard pattern from #3423 to logger levels and handlers, the quiet flag and the tracer provider.
